source: WHO, Pregnancy, Childbirth, Postpartum and Newborn Care: a guide for essential practice (PCPNC, 3rd ed., 2015); WHO, Managing Complications in Pregnancy and Childbirth (MCPC, 2nd ed., 2017); WHO recommendations for the prevention and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage (2012).

magnesium_sulfate.label: Magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) 50% — pre-referral loading dose
magnesium_sulfate.dose: 10 g IM: 5 g (10 ml of 50%) deep IM in each buttock, with 1 ml of 2% lidocaine in the same syringe
magnesium_sulfate.how: one time, then transfer immediately; only by a trained health worker
magnesium_sulfate.for: convulsions or signs of severe pre-eclampsia

oxytocin.label: Oxytocin
oxytocin.how: one injection, then transfer immediately; only by a trained health worker
oxytocin.for: heavy bleeding after birth or placenta not delivered

misoprostol.label: Misoprostol 200 microgram tablets
misoprostol.how: one time, only if oxytocin is not available and the baby is already born; then transfer immediately
misoprostol.for: heavy bleeding after birth when oxytocin is not available
